text: Thanks — I can reproduce the report: `required=True` is silently ignored for boolean flags. I'm tracing the root cause now (it's in how `Option` assigns a default of `False` to flags, which makes the required check think a value was supplied). ETA ~10 minutes to have it fixed and verified against the test suite.

Got it — that's a separate bug: on Windows with `pythonw.exe` there's no console, and `click.echo` (plus the progress bar and pager) doesn't guard against the missing stdout handle, so it raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'`. I'll make those paths silently no-op when there's no console. I'm finishing the required-flag fix first, then this one. ETA ~20 min.

Confirmed: for a flag with `flag_value` and `envvar`, the raw env var text is used as the value instead of `flag_value`. I'm fixing it so the env var acts as a switch (value = `flag_value`), while keeping boolean flags like `--on/--off` parsing the env var as a boolean. ETA ~8 min.

Confirmed: the `argument`/`option` decorators pop `cls` out of the shared attributes dict, so a decorator reused on a second command silently falls back to the default class. I'm making the decorators non-destructive so reuse keeps your custom class. ETA ~8 min.

Confirmed: `Path(resolve_path=True)` reads the symlink target and then resolves it against the current working directory, so relative symlink targets come out wrong. I'm switching that resolution to a proper path resolution that handles relative targets. ETA ~8 min.

Confirmed: the help record builds the flag's default string from the option's own default only, ignoring `default_map`. I'm making it use the effective default (default map first), so `--help` will show `default: name` when your default map sets it to `True`. ETA ~8 min.
